 --> 8th Pay Commission: Fitment factor demands range from 3.61 to 4; how much could basic pay rise?
 The actual salary revision will ultimately depend on the fitment factor recommended under the 8th Pay Commission and the final structure approved by the government. 
 Dipen Pradhan 
 November 17, 2026 / 16:05 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Unions demand fitment factors ranging from 3.61 to 4.00.
 Minimum basic pay could rise significantly under 8th CPC.
 Higher basic pay will also increase HRA and pensions.

 The 8th Central Pay Commission has concluded its regional consultation tour across states and Union Territories, with the final meetings held in Bengaluru on October 7–8 and Mumbai on October 22–23.
 The Commission is now expected to focus on analysing stakeholder submissions and drafting its recommendations. Its report, anticipated around May 2027, will propose revisions to the pay and pension structures of 50.14 lakh central government employees and around 69 lakh pensioners.
 Meanwhile, attention is turning to whether the government can accommodate the steep fitment factors sought by employee organisations. A fitment factor determines the multiplier applied to existing basic pay to calculate revised salaries. 
 The NC-JCM Staff Side (National Council – Joint Consultative Machinery), for instance, has demanded a fitment factor of 3.833, which would raise the minimum basic pay to Rs 68,994 per month. 
 The BPMS (Bhartiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh), a defence workers' union, has sought a higher fitment factor of 4.00, translating into a minimum basic pay of Rs 72,000 per month. Meanwhile, the Ministerial Staff Association (MSA) has proposed a fitment factor of 3.61, which would take the minimum basic pay to Rs 64,980 per month.

 Here is how the basic pay of central government employees across Pay Levels 1 to 18 could change under these proposed fitment factors. 
 That being said, the actual revision in basic pay will depend on the 8th Pay Commission's recommendations and the government's final approval. 
 For employees at Level 1, whose current entry basic pay was fixed at Rs 18,000 under the 7th Pay Commission, a fitment factor of 3.61 would raise the basic pay to Rs 64,980. At 3.833, it would increase to Rs 68,994, while a factor of 4.00 would take it to Rs 72,000. Similarly, for Level 10 employees, with a starting basic pay of Rs 56,100, the revised basic pay would rise to Rs 2,02,521 at a fitment factor of 3.61, Rs 2,15,031 at 3.833 and Rs 2,24,400 at 4.00. At the highest pay level, where the current entry basic pay is Rs 2.50 lakh, a fitment factor of 3.61 would take it to Rs 9,02,500. The basic pay would increase to Rs 9,58,250 at 3.833 and Rs 10 lakh at a fitment factor of 4.00. Read more : CPI inflation breaches 6%; will it strengthen demands for higher fitment factor? According to pension experts, the challenge for the 8th CPC extends beyond salary revisions, as the Central government also contributes to retirement schemes for millions of employees. Besides increasing salaries, it would also raise contributions to pension schemes, which are linked to employees' basic pay and dearness allowance. A revision in basic pay could also translate into higher allowances, particularly House Rent Allowance (HRA), which is calculated as a percentage of basic pay. Under the 7th Pay Commission framework, HRA rates vary depending on an employee's place of posting, with cities classified into X, Y and Z categories. Employees posted in X-category cities receive the highest HRA, followed by those in Y- and Z-category cities. Read more : Projected house rent allowance for central government employees at different fitment factors Although the fitment factor does not directly determine an employee’s HRA, it increases the basic pay on which the allowance is calculated. The actual salary and HRA revision will ultimately depend on the fitment factor recommended under the 8th Pay Commission and the final structure approved by the government.
